Soojin / Lauren — quick ops note to confirm how we route:

- Invoice path: commit line items are created on our billing system as Distributor-Payable rows. In practice we generate an invoice to the distributor (Distributor X) with two line types: COMMIT_SKU (list-price) and COMMIT_CREDIT (negative line for passback). The distributor invoice then nets to the reseller according to the passback % that is stored against the SKU.

- Credits / overages: Overages are billed monthly to HealthLynx (end-customer) at the list price with a memo that references the commit. We reconcile monthly and post a settlement that adjusts the distributor invoice in the following billing cycle.

- Regional brokerage: We can split passback at the SKU level by territory tag. Example: SKU-A --- US East 6% / US West 5% / EMEA 7%. We store the percentage in the passback table and include the calculated brokerage in the invoice line item so your AP system sees the net flow.

Attached a quick calculation workbook (brokerage_calc_v2.xlsx) with a sample for the phased commit you requested (40/30/30). Notes: the phasing affects timing of when distributor invoices are released, not the total committed amount.

Soojin — suggest we send Anna a single-page worked example plus the CSV and the brokerage_calc file. Anna — if you want, we can also produce an anonymized sample invoice PDF to show the exact row structure.

Ben
Channel Operations
Redwood Inference

Anna — following up with the package we discussed. Please find attached: commit-phasing-proposal.pdf (one-page worked example), passback_mapping.csv (SKU -> territory -> %), and brokerage_calc_v2.xlsx (calculation workbook). Summary below: 

- Invoice path summary: Distributor invoice is generated at the time we recognize the committed portion for a region. Each invoice contains: SKU line (gross), brokerage line (negative to reflect passback), and a settlement memo referencing the HealthLynx PO. Overages billed separately monthly to HealthLynx; settlements then adjust distributor invoices in the next cycle.

- Staggered timing: For the 40/30/30 split you proposed, Distributor X will receive three invoices aligned to the phasing quarters. Total committed value remains unchanged; phasing only shifts recognition/invoicing timing for distributor passbacks.

- Regional mapping: We included a CSV mapping for the three regions (US East / US West / EMEA). If the reseller is a single global reseller but invoices regionally, use the territory tag on the SKU row. If you have multiple regional resellers, update the CSV with the reseller ID column we provided.

Next steps:
1) Confirm whether you want an anonymized PDF of a full distributor invoice layout (we can produce today).
2) If the CSV looks good, share the upload target for your reconciliation system or we can push it to your SFTP.
3) If you approve, we will add the finalized passback mapping to the deal and flag the invoice routing to operations.

Proposed quick call: Thu 9am PT to finalize the CSV and invoice example. I can send a calendar invite once you confirm.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this across the finish line.

Best,
Soojin Lee
